node-1.label: A 13-year-old girl experienced joint pain, subcutaneous nodules, and difficulty breathing over the past three months.

node-2.label: 13-year-old girl had joint pain for three months, gradually affecting knees, ankles, elbows, wrists, and fingers bilaterally, more on the right side, worsening over time, severe at night and early morning, causing missed school, with swelling and redness around the joints; initially responsive to Ibuprofen but later ineffective.

node-3.label: Two months after joint pain onset, her mother noticed small, round, non-tender, skin-colored subcutaneous nodules on her elbows and arms; on examination, subcutaneous nodules were present on the extensor surface of the right elbow and interphalangeal joints, with no signs of arthritis.

node-4.label: She subsequently developed chest pain and exertional difficulty breathing that worsened when lying down; vital signs were temperature 37ºC, respiratory rate 28/min, heart rate 129/min, blood pressure 126/70 mmHg; height 153 cm, weight 81 kg, BMI 35.

node-5.label: Cardiovascular examination revealed a grade 3 holosystolic murmur with highest intensity at the apex; she exhibited an antalgic gait.

node-6.label: She had an upper respiratory tract infection and high fever (39-40ºC) two weeks before the joint pain, lasting one week and improving with antipyretics; she had no recent palpitations, rash, coughing up blood, mood swings, or abnormal movements; she visited multiple healthcare facilities before referral and was admitted for management and further investigation.

attrs.why: node-2 polyarthritis, node-3 subcutaneous nodules, node-4-5 carditis/dyspnea/murmur, node-6 antecedent febrile URI all support acute rheumatic fever.
node-4-6 fever/dyspnea/murmur/antecedent infection support IE; node-2 chronic polyarthritis and node-3 subcutaneous nodules argue against.
node-2 chronic morning joint pain/swelling and node-3 subcutaneous nodules support inflammatory arthritis; cardiac murmur/dyspnea less typical.

attrs.why: New laboratory and imaging evidence strengthen the diagnosis: ESR 120 and CRP 2.3 indicate marked inflammation, ASO 832 confirms antecedent group A streptococcal infection, and echocardiography shows severe mitral regurgitation, mild aortic regurgitation, and mild pericardial effusion. Both laboratory and radiology experts agree that these findings, along with the polyarthritis and subcutaneous nodules, meet Jones criteria for rheumatic fever with carditis. Confidence increases from 0.86 to 0.96.

Infective endocarditis becomes much less likely: the high ASO titer of 832 points to post-streptococcal rheumatic fever rather than IE, and the chronic polyarthritis and subcutaneous nodules argue against IE. Although echocardiographic valve regurgitation and pericardial effusion can occur in IE, the overall picture and expert analyses favor rheumatic carditis. Confidence decreases from 0.12 to 0.04.

Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is less likely because the new ASO 832 and echocardiographic valvular involvement (severe mitral regurgitation, mild aortic regurgitation, pericardial effusion) are atypical for JIA and better explain rheumatic carditis. Chronic joint symptoms and nodules still provide some support, but expert analyses consider JIA unlikely. Confidence decreases from 0.25 to 0.10.
